full_judgment: 4. On the other hand, Mr Md Modersher Ali Khan (Dipu), the learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the respondents-government by filing affidavit-in-opposition and supplementary affidavit to the affidavit-in-opposition submits that the petitioner by giving false declaration imported contraband goods through illegal way and had tried to release those goods in an unlawful manner, which is a violation of section. 32 of the Customs Act, 1969 read with section 3(1) of the Export. and Import Control Act, 1950 as well as and section 8(1) of the Foreign Exchange Regulations Act, 1947, Para 26 of the Import Police Order 2015-2018, section 25B of the Special Power Act, 1974 and section 2(Sha)(18) of the Money Laundering Act, 1012. Accordingly, he submits that said alleged act of the petitioner being punishable under Clauses 8/9(i) and 14 of section 156(1) of the Act, 1959 the Customs authority lodged Bandar Police Station Case No.11(12)16 corresponding to GR No.289/16(Kha) against the petitioner's company along with other accused persons and that said case is still pending. As such, he submits that since allegations so brought against the petitioner are grievous in nature and are punishable offence, considering the said circumstances the Customs authority locked the BIN of the company until finalizing the inquiry so had been initiated by the said authority. However, fact remains that when process of show cause was pending in the meantime the petitioner filed this writ petition and obtained the ad-interim order passed by this Hon'ble Court with direction to unlock the BIN of the petitioner's company and in compliances thereof BIN has been unlocked.
